rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXVII If the Estate of the Native shall continue, or be Durable
rules.meaning_historical_only: Printed CXVII begins after a divider on the lower part of original PDF596; asks whether financial resources endure.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: principal Significators of Substance
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly bases endurance of estate on the principal wealth significators defined earlier, not solely the second-house cusp.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: he is ever that Planet who is posited in the second
rules.meaning_historical_only: The source initially prioritizes a planet physically in the second house for assessing durability.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if essentially dignified
rules.meaning_historical_only: The second-house planet's essential dignity is an explicit condition and cannot be ignored when selecting its signification.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if this Planet be benevolent
rules.meaning_historical_only: A naturally or contextually benevolent second-house occupant is one component of the favorable case.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: powerfull
rules.meaning_historical_only: The occupant must also possess strength; the source does not treat planetary identity as sufficient.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: essentially qualified in dignities
rules.meaning_historical_only: Essential dignities are additionally required for the author's strongest wealth-persistence prediction.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: his Wealth will continue and remain without any disturbance
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly alleges continued resources without disruption under the compound favorable state; no financial observation is supplied.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: all his life time
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author describes an alleged lifelong property outcome rather than a one-year forecast, with no observation window.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If that Planet be weak
rules.meaning_historical_only: When the selected second-house occupant is weak, Lilly gives a different mixed durability result.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: his Riches will continue, but with great hazard
rules.meaning_historical_only: Weakness is said to allow property to continue but with instability rather than automatically vanish.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: much difficulty to attaine ... great labour to preserve
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author alleges increased effort both to acquire and retain property under this natal condition.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: get good store of Wealth
rules.meaning_historical_only: Temporary accumulation of substantial wealth remains compatible with the negative/weak profile.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: suddenly again shall lose somewhat equivalent
rules.meaning_historical_only: Sudden losses roughly equal to gains are allowed despite continued overall wealth, making precise scoring difficult.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If an Infortune be in the second
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly singles out a malefic occupying the second house, without declaring its mere presence categorically ruinous.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: consider if he be strong or weak
rules.meaning_historical_only: The dignity/strength of a second-house malefic decides between alternative outcomes.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if he be potent, the estate shall continue
rules.meaning_historical_only: A strong malefic is alleged to allow resources to persist, contradicting an unconditional negative Saturn/Mars rule.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: but with difficulty
rules.meaning_historical_only: In that strong-malefic branch, the continuation is explicitly qualified as difficult.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: subject rather to lose then lay up
rules.meaning_historical_only: The source predicts accumulation impediments even with resources persisting.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if he be unfortunate, his Fortune shall not continue
rules.meaning_historical_only: An unfortunate/debilitated malefic is assigned a contrary lack-of-continuation result.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: be overthrown and come to nothing
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly's maximal loss claim is described in absolute terms but has no external case proof.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: moderately fortified, frame your judgment accordingly
rules.meaning_historical_only: Intermediate dignities are assigned an unfixed intermediate outcome; the author gives no calibration.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If many Planets be in the second house
rules.meaning_historical_only: The source explicitly contemplates more than one occupying planet, requiring a prioritization rule.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: most powerfull
rules.meaning_historical_only: Among multiple second-house planets, the most powerful takes precedence rather than being averaged.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: according unto whose nature ... judge
rules.meaning_historical_only: The preferred planet's nature then conditions the durability judgment, a separate step after strength ranking.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If no Planet be in the second
rules.meaning_historical_only: An empty second house is an explicitly recognized common case rather than automatic missing evidence.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the second house
rules.meaning_historical_only: The second-house ruler becomes a fallback significator when the second has no occupant.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Dispositor of Part of Fortune
rules.meaning_historical_only: The Part of Fortune dispositor is also named in the empty-second fallback, with ranking among the two not explicit.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: thereafter consider of Wealth or poverty
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author uses those fallback factors to resume general financial evaluation rather than assigning a blank chart.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: About what part of his life ... expect Wealth
rules.meaning_historical_only: The chapter separately asks when in the life course the gain could occur rather than merely if the estate continues.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators and Part of Fortune directed
rules.meaning_historical_only: Directions of wealth significators and Part of Fortune are offered as the preferred time calculation.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: to Beneficall Promittors
rules.meaning_historical_only: Favorable planetary promittors are stated targets of directions; their identity requires freezing in a real test.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: to Sextile Trine or [ambiguous symbol]
rules.meaning_historical_only: The source mentions apparently sextile, trine and one difficult-to-distinguish aspect marker in the timing string; preserve the glyph uncertainty rather than assert a precise algorithm.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the second
rules.meaning_historical_only: The second-house ruler is a listed timing target separate from any second-house occupant.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Dispositor of Part of Fortune
rules.meaning_historical_only: The dispositor of Part of Fortune is another possible directed contact, permitting multiple timing opportunities.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: or Planet in the second
rules.meaning_historical_only: Planets actually in the second house also supply possible targets, distinct from house ruler or Fortune dispositor.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: and their severall aspects
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly permits various aspects of these targets, with no stated fixed tolerance or penalty for multiple tests.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: in what quarter of Heaven ... Significators
rules.meaning_historical_only: As a less exact general timing alternative, Lilly uses the house quadrant containing the strong wealth significators.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: especially him that is most fortified
rules.meaning_historical_only: The strongest significator is weighted preferentially for general life-stage timing.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: betwixt the ascendant and tenth house ... youth
rules.meaning_historical_only: If the relevant significators lie between the Ascendant and tenth house, Lilly alleges wealth increases during youth.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: ninth eighth or seventh ... Manhood
rules.meaning_historical_only: Placement in the ninth, eighth or seventh house is assigned a later life phase of wealth gain.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: full age ... twenty five to thirty five or forty
rules.meaning_historical_only: The second phase includes a broad author-defined age interval extending roughly 25 to 35 or 40.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: sixth fifth or fourth ... nearer old age
rules.meaning_historical_only: The sixth, fifth and fourth houses are assigned a further phase toward old age.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: after forty ... before fifty five
rules.meaning_historical_only: The older phase is described as after 40 but before 55, overlapping a preceding age band.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: third second or first ... latter end
rules.meaning_historical_only: The third, second and first houses are associated with the later part of the person's life.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: whether the Native ... live many or few yeers
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author says to adapt the life-phase timing to a prediction of the native's longevity, adding model flexibility.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: divide that time ... point out ... accesse to Riches
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly further permits subdividing the alleged lifespan to refine timing, but gives no independently calibrated method.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators Orientall of the Sun ... time sooner
rules.meaning_historical_only: Wealth significators oriental to the Sun are alleged to accelerate the expected event time.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Occidentall ... nearer old age
rules.meaning_historical_only: Occidental significators are said to delay the outcome toward later age.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Retrograde Planets ... retard
rules.meaning_historical_only: Retrograde motion is separately said to postpone expected financial gains.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: direct and swift in motion ... hasten
rules.meaning_historical_only: Direct and swift motion is said to hasten events, a conditional alternative to retrograde delay.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: If Directions concurre with ... time limited
rules.meaning_historical_only: Concurrence between directional events and the earlier life-phase estimate is said to increase the interpreter's confidence.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: prove more certain ... confident
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly asserts increased reliability from agreement among his own calculations, but gives no blind evidence of calibration.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn Mars or [glyph unresolved] ... ill posited in the second
rules.meaning_historical_only: Poorly placed malefics or another source glyph in the second are alleged adverse; the last glyph must be independently verified.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the second Combust
rules.meaning_historical_only: The second-house ruler combust is a further adverse condition, not an automatic conclusion from Saturn in the second.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Part of Fortune unfortunate
rules.meaning_historical_only: Affliction of Part of Fortune is separately named with the second-house ruler debility.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: confiscation of Estate banishment
rules.meaning_historical_only: The historical author asserts severe property/legal harms, but this is not evidence of criminality or actual legal outcomes.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Luminaries applying to Planets in angles
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly gives a condition in which the Sun/Moon apply to planets occupying angular houses.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: continues in Estate ... left by Ancestors
rules.meaning_historical_only: Under angular applications the author alleges continuing roughly in the financial state inherited from one's ancestors.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if they apply to Planets in cadent houses
rules.meaning_historical_only: Applications to planets in cadent houses form an opposite conditional case.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: diminisheth his Paternal stock
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author alleges reducing the paternal estate for cadent applications, not an objectively demonstrated outcome.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Oculus Tauri, Cor Scorpionis, Caput Medusae
rules.meaning_historical_only: Three named fixed stars/asterisms are cited as allegedly harmful wealth indicators; the original glyphs and fixed-star ephemerides remain unverified.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: with Part of Fortune or joyned to his Lord
rules.meaning_historical_only: These stars/points must be in a specified relationship with Part of Fortune or its ruler; exact geometry is absent.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: loss of Riches ... threatens poverty
rules.meaning_historical_only: The historical text associates the fixed-star configuration with loss of estate and poverty, without actual event records.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: estate designed by Saturn ... covetous
rules.meaning_historical_only: Lilly asserts a covetous personality for Saturn-dominated estate sources; this stereotype is not a person-level character finding.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: when Sun and Moon have signification, then not so
rules.meaning_historical_only: The same stereotype is said not to hold under solar/lunar estate signification, showing another source-internal exception.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Infortunes behold the Significator of Substance
rules.meaning_historical_only: The source names hostile aspect(s) from malefics to a main estate significator as a prerequisite.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: both be Retrograde
rules.meaning_historical_only: Retrograde motion of both referents is an additional requirement whose exact plural antecedent needs review.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Cadent
rules.meaning_historical_only: Cadency is separately part of the adverse multi-factor condition.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Peregrine
rules.meaning_historical_only: Peregrine state is also present and cannot be silently equated with retrograde or cadent status.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: in Signes of contrary nature
rules.meaning_historical_only: Placement in opposed/contrary-nature signs further qualifies the complex negative condition.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Native will be perpetually poor
rules.meaning_historical_only: The author claims lifelong poverty under the compound configuration, without numeric wealth/age thresholds or any verified example.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Judgments upon the third House Of Kinred, viz. Brethren and Sisters
rules.meaning_historical_only: An unnumbered third-house introduction begins after the decorative divider on source PDF598, distinct from the preceding wealth chapter.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Nativity of the first borne
rules.meaning_historical_only: The following introductory paragraph recommends the oldest sibling's nativity for counting younger siblings; its substantive rules are not admitted in this wealth batch.

rules.original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXVIII If have Brethren or Sisters
rules.meaning_historical_only: The next printed numbered chapter opens lower on original PDF598, following the unnumbered third-house introduction, and continues into PDF599.
